title: Revive Us Again
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Revival begins in each heart. Every morning the battle for your allegiance begins again, so cry out, "Lord, revive me," and trust a God who keeps every promise.
exhortation: This is our 100th episode of Worship Is Warfare. We do this so that our eyes would be set on Christ. The one aim this morning is that our hearts would be set on fire with the glory and majesty of Jesus.

So what is revival? Revival begins in the heart of every one of us. What will command our devotion and our love? What will we worship? Every morning the battle begins anew for the allegiance of your heart. Will you be consumed with the cares of this world, or does your heart cry out like the psalmist, "Lord, revive me"? When your heart is cold, does it cry, "I'm not satisfied with a dead and cold heart. I must have you"?
"Let me hear what God the Lord will speak." I don't want my own words or my own thoughts. I don't want the cravings of this world or the chatter of ungodliness. I want your words. Lord, revive me.

And then from verse 10 the confidence grows: "Steadfast love and faithfulness meet; righteousness and peace kiss each other." There has never been a promise the Lord has not kept. When Jesus ascended, he promised us his Spirit, and he gave him. He told us the work was finished, and it was. We serve a God who keeps his promises. If his people will come and repent and turn from their folly and not go back, his promises are sure. So this morning the prayer is this: Lord Jesus, help us return to you. Help us not to go back to our folly, but to pursue you wholeheartedly.
prayer: Lord, we are so grateful for such a great salvation: one that doesn't just wash us clean and send us off on our own, but brings us into relationship with you. You never leave us or forsake us. When we stumble, you are there to lift us up. You revive us again and again, and reaffirm your steadfast love and faithfulness: what you started, you will complete. Your yes will always be yes, and in Christ all the promises of God are yes and amen.

Thank you for showing us this grace and opening our eyes. Remind us again that it wasn't our faithfulness that saved us. It was yours. So in your faithfulness and steadfast love we gladly depend. In Jesus' name, amen.
